title: Describing People and Characters

dialogue.title: Describing Family Members
dialogue.context: Ahmed shows his coworkers photos of his family and describes each person.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Ahmed, are these your family photos? Tell us about them!

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes! This is my mother. She's in her fifties, average height, and she has kind eyes. She's always smiling.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: She looks very warm and friendly. What's her personality like?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: She's incredibly patient and generous. She used to help all the neighbors in Somalia. Everyone loved her.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: And who's this tall man next to her?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That's my older brother, Abdi. He's about six feet tall with a athletic build. He played soccer professionally.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: He looks serious in this photo.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: He can be serious about work, but he has a great sense of humor with family. He's also very protective of our younger siblings.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That's my niece, Amina. She has big brown eyes and curly hair. She's only seven but very curious and talkative. She asks a million questions!

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: She sounds adorable! Who does she remind you of?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Actually, she reminds me of my mother - same curious nature and warm personality. People say I was like that as a child too.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: It's wonderful how family traits get passed down. You must miss them so much.

examples: He is of average height with a muscular build.
She is in her thirties with long black hair.
He is short with broad shoulders.
She is elderly with gray hair and glasses.
She has curly brown hair and green eyes.
He has a beard and wears glasses.
She has a warm smile and dimples.
He has dark skin and short hair.
She has freckles and red hair.

listening_exercises.transcript: When describing people, separate appearance from personality. For appearance, describe: height (tall, short, average), build (slim, athletic, heavy-set), age (young, middle-aged, elderly), and distinct features (hair color, eye color, facial hair). For personality, use adjectives like: friendly, shy, outgoing, serious, funny, kind, patient. Be specific and respectful.
listening_exercises.question: What should you describe separately?

listening_exercises.transcript: Avoid stereotypes when describing people. Don't assume someone's personality based on their appearance, nationality, or profession. Instead of 'All teachers are patient,' say 'My teacher is patient.' Instead of 'She looks mean,' say 'She looks serious.' Focus on what you actually observe or know about the specific person.
listening_exercises.question: How should you avoid stereotypes?
options: Focus on the specific person, not groups

listening_exercises.transcript: Using 'tends to' or 'usually' shows nuance in descriptions. 'She tends to be quiet in large groups' is more accurate than 'She is quiet.' 'He's usually cheerful' acknowledges that moods change. This makes your descriptions more realistic and shows you understand that people are complex.
listening_exercises.question: Why use 'tends to' or 'usually'?
options: To show people are complex and moods change

speaking_tasks.prompt: Describe someone important in your life. Include both appearance and personality. Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I want to describe my best friend from home. Her name is Fatima. She's in her late twenties, about average height, and she has beautiful long black hair that she usually wears in a braid. She has dark brown eyes and a contagious smile. As for her personality, Fatima is one of the most loyal and supportive people I know. She's always there when I need to talk. She tends to be quiet in groups, but one-on-one she's very open and funny. What I admire most about her is her strength - she always stays positive even during difficult times.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Compare two people you know - how are they similar and different in appearance or personality? Record for 25 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: My two brothers are very different. My older brother Abdi is tall and athletic, while my younger brother Hassan is shorter and slimmer. In personality, they're also opposites. Abdi is very serious and responsible - he always thinks before acting. Hassan is more spontaneous and fun-loving. However, they're similar in one important way - both are extremely loyal to family. They would do anything to help each other or our parents.

writing_tasks.prompt: Describe a family member or close friend. Include physical appearance, personality, and what makes them special. (80-100 words)
writing_tasks.example: My mother is the most important person in my life. She's in her mid-fifties, with graying hair that she keeps in a traditional headscarf. She has a round, kind face with warm brown eyes that crinkle when she smiles. Physically, she's of average height but very strong from years of hard work. Her personality is what makes her truly special. She's incredibly patient - I never saw her lose her temper, even in difficult situations. She's also very generous and always puts others before herself. What I admire most is her wisdom. She always knows the right thing to say when I'm struggling. She has this quiet strength that inspires everyone around her. I miss her every day.

writing_tasks.prompt: Describe a character from a book, movie, or TV show. What do they look like? What's their personality? (60-80 words)
writing_tasks.example: One of my favorite characters is Forrest Gump from the movie. He's a tall man with short brown hair and a simple, honest face. Throughout the movie, he wears casual clothes and often carries his suitcase. His personality is what makes him special - he's incredibly kind, loyal, and optimistic. He tends to see the good in everyone. Even though people said he wasn't smart, he achieved amazing things through his determination and good heart. His simple wisdom often revealed deep truths.

grammar_focus.title: 'Be + adjective' for Appearance and Personality
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'be + adjective' to describe how someone is.

grammar_focus.title: 'Have/has + features' for Physical Characteristics
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'have/has' to talk about physical features someone possesses.

grammar_focus.title: Relative Clauses with 'who' for People
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'who' to add information about a person.
examples: My mother, who lives in Somalia, is very kind. (extra info)
The man who helped me was very friendly. (identifying which man)
She's the teacher who taught me English. (identifying which teacher)
My friend, who I met in class, is from Mexico. (extra info)

practice.sentence: The person ___ helped me was kind.
My sister, ___ lives here, is tall.
He's the man ___ I told you about.

questions.question: How does Ahmed describe his mother?
What sport did Ahmed's brother play?
How old is Ahmed's niece Amina?
You should avoid stereotypes when describing people.
It's okay to assume someone's personality from their appearance.
The person ___ helped me was kind. (relative clause)
Who does Amina remind Ahmed of?

vocabulary.example: He has a warm, friendly personality.
Her eyes are her most striking feature.

cultural_notes: In American culture, commenting on someone's appearance can be sensitive. Focus on compliments like 'You look nice' rather than specific body features.
It's common to describe personality traits when introducing people: 'This is my friend Sarah - she's really funny and creative.'
Americans value individuality and don't like being stereotyped based on groups they belong to.
When describing people in professional contexts, focus on relevant qualities and accomplishments, not appearance.
Physical descriptions are used mainly for practical purposes (helping someone find a person) or in close relationships.
Describing someone as 'interesting' or 'unique' is usually a compliment in American culture.
